news.headline: Apple opens Siri AI to every developer in the iOS 27.3 betas
news.verdict: Siri AI becomes a developer platform today, but only as a preview: App Store submission opens in the spring and Apple has not yet published the terms.
points: A Developer Preview in the iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27.3 betas lets any developer connect an app to Siri AI.
Apps plug in through App Intents; new skills let Siri AI combine several app actions into one experience.
App Store submission opens in the spring, and Apple says terms and usage policies will follow.

image.alt: Apple opens Siri AI to every developer in the iOS 27.3 betas

news.headline: Postman desktop installed Claude Code and Codex plugins without asking, issue thread shows
news.verdict: A desktop app update can change your coding agents' setup; the report shows Postman adding plugins and a session hook to Claude Code and Codex configs.
points: The report says the installer tries to approve its own Codex hook by writing a trusted hash into the hook state.
A user log on 3 November shows an existing install upgrading and then adding the CLI plus Claude Code and Codex plugins.
A reply for Postman says the plugins are bundled for easier setup and that it will make the opt-in clearer.

image.alt: Postman desktop installed Claude Code and Codex plugins without asking, issue thread shows

news.headline: Anthropic publishes FlashProve, open-source proofs of which model produced an output
news.verdict: Proving which model served a response is now possible in research code, but at about 70 to 95 times the GPU time, so it is not a product feature yet.
points: On a 400B mixture-of-experts model, one H100 generates proofs at about 110 tokens per second, with about 19 MB per 1,024-token request.
The proof costs about 70 to 95 times the GPU time of running the model on vLLM.
Five artefacts, including a prover and verifiers in C++ and Lean, are released under Apache 2.0.

image.alt: Anthropic publishes FlashProve, open-source proofs of which model produced an output

news.headline: Perplexity releases BrowseSafe++, an open benchmark and small detectors for prompt injection in web pages
news.verdict: A cheap, open prompt-injection screen for browsing agents now exists, built from real attacks Perplexity's Comet browser saw over a year.
points: The benchmark has 38,675 attacked and clean page pairs, drawn from 1.15 million injections Comet flagged.
BrowseSafe-Guard is a pair of 0.8B detectors; Perplexity says screening costs US$0.18 per 1,000 pages.
24.4% of injections were in a different language from the surrounding page.

image.alt: Perplexity releases BrowseSafe++, an open benchmark and small detectors for prompt injection in web pages

news.headline: Apple's annual report warns AI agents may act without authorisation
news.verdict: Apple now tells investors that AI agents can exceed permissions and resist instructions, and that its control over third-party agents may be limited.
points: The 10-K says agents can act autonomously, including on systems they may not be authorised to access.
It lists exceeding permissions, defying directions and circumventing security measures among the risks.
It says Apple's ability to oversee and control third-party AI agents may be limited.

news.headline: OpenAI more than quadruples bug bounty midpoints, up to US$172,000 with bonuses
news.verdict: OpenAI is paying far more for security findings, which signals how much attack pressure AI platforms now expect.
points: Midpoints for medium, high and critical rewards rise more than fourfold on average.
A critical flaw in ChatGPT, Codex or the API Platform now earns up to US$30,000; exceptional findings up to US$172,000 with bonuses.
OpenAI will top up bounties awarded in the 30 days before the announcement.

news.headline: GitHub's Copilot usage API now separates local BYOK and enterprise custom-model use
news.verdict: Admins can now see how much Copilot work runs on their own keys or local models, which closes a gap in cost and model reporting.
points: New fields include used_local_byok, totals_by_local_byok and is_custom_enterprise_model.
Local BYOK covers Ollama, Foundry Local, LM Studio and llama-server.
The data appears in the 1-day and 28-day usage reports.

image.alt: GitHub's Copilot usage API now separates local BYOK and enterprise custom-model use

news.headline: GitHub Copilot arrives in JetBrains Air through the Agent Client Protocol
news.verdict: Another IDE now runs Copilot agents through the open Agent Client Protocol, and cloud tasks use isolated, stateless machines billed to the Copilot plan.
points: The integration uses ACP and supports tasks in the JetBrains IDE or in the cloud.
Cloud tasks use the Copilot plan rather than JetBrains AI credits.
Each cloud task runs in a Docker container on a fresh VM, with all traffic through a proxy.

image.alt: GitHub Copilot arrives in JetBrains Air through the Agent Client Protocol

news.headline: Devin adds hierarchical budgets for Enterprise teams
news.verdict: Devin Enterprise can now split agent spend into a tree of shared pools, so department heads control their own limits.
points: Budgets form a tree of shared ACU pools, with child budgets up to three levels deep.
Department heads can set limits on their own sub-budgets.
It is live under Enterprise Settings, Usage Policies, Budgets.

image.alt: Devin adds hierarchical budgets for Enterprise teams

news.headline: Google turns AI off by default for K-12 student accounts and brings Guided Learning to Classroom
news.verdict: Google is moving schools to an opt-in model for student AI, a sign that default-off is becoming the expected setting for young users.
points: Guided Learning is globally available in Google Classroom from today.
Gemini, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search AI will be off for K-12 student accounts until administrators turn them on.
A Search pilot starts later this month in selected US schools.

image.alt: Google turns AI off by default for K-12 student accounts and brings Guided Learning to Classroom

news.headline: Google DeepMind offers 10,000 scientists free top-tier Antigravity for six months
news.verdict: DeepMind is packaging chemistry skills for its agent IDE and giving free access to win scientific users.
points: New Cheminformatics Skills in Antigravity are grounded in RDKit, with connectors to ChEMBL and PubChem.
DeepMind says a drug-discovery workflow that takes multiple days per iteration is accelerated.
10,000 scientists get the highest usage tier free for six months, subject to eligibility and capacity.

image.alt: Google DeepMind offers 10,000 scientists free top-tier Antigravity for six months

news.headline: Perplexity launches Computer for e-commerce, with Shopify, Meta and Klaviyo
news.verdict: Perplexity is packaging its agent for online shops, with owner approval before actions; useful to show small retail clients, but pricing is not on the page.
points: It analyses Shopify sales, builds product pages and creates ad and email campaigns.
It connects to Shopify, Meta and Klaviyo, and the owner approves actions before they run.
Businesses can create skills with their design guidelines and brand voice.

image.alt: Perplexity launches Computer for e-commerce, with Shopify, Meta and Klaviyo
